prompt: A user's PC shows a screen stating all files are encrypted and demands Bitcoin payment. What type of malware is this?
explanation: Ransomware encrypts files and demands payment. The best defense is offline backups (3-2-1 rule). Do not pay if avoidable — payment funds future attacks and doesn't guarantee recovery.

prompt: A technician needs to force Group Policy settings to apply immediately without rebooting. Which command should they use?
explanation: gpupdate /force immediately refreshes and applies all Group Policy settings. gpresult shows the resultant policy. gpedit.msc opens the Group Policy editor.

prompt: A Windows PC cannot browse websites by name but can ping IP addresses successfully. What is the MOST likely cause?
explanation: If IP connectivity works but name resolution fails, DNS is the issue. Run nslookup to verify. Check the DNS server IP in network adapter settings — it may point to an incorrect server.

prompt: A user reports that a caller claiming to be from IT called asking for their password to fix a problem. What type of attack is this?
explanation: Vishing = Voice phishing via phone call. Phishing = email. Smishing = SMS text. Tailgating = physical access. IT departments should NEVER ask for your password.

prompt: Which file system supports file permissions, encryption, compression, and files larger than 4GB?
explanation: NTFS supports all these features. FAT32 is limited to 4GB file size. exFAT supports large files but lacks permissions and encryption. NTFS is the standard for Windows system drives.

prompt: A user's laptop gets an IP address of 169.254.12.55. What does this indicate?

options.text: The DHCP server assigned this manually
DHCP failed and Windows assigned an APIPA address

explanation: 169.254.x.x is an APIPA (Automatic Private IP Addressing) address. Windows self-assigns this when no DHCP server responds. It allows only link-local communication — no internet access.

prompt: Which backup type backs up only the data changed since the LAST FULL backup and does NOT reset the archive bit?
explanation: Differential backup captures changes since the last full backup. It does NOT reset the archive bit (unlike full and incremental). To restore: need only the latest full + latest differential.

prompt: A company requires that users can only access corporate WiFi with individual credentials (not a shared password). Which technology enables this?
explanation: WPA2-Enterprise with 802.1X uses a RADIUS server for per-user authentication. Each user logs in with their unique credentials. WPA2-Personal uses a shared PSK (pre-shared key) password.

prompt: A user reports that their Windows 10 Home PC cannot connect to the company domain. What is the cause?

options.text: Windows 10 Home does not support domain join
The PC needs to be restarted

explanation: Windows 10/11 Home cannot join an Active Directory domain — only Pro and Enterprise support domain join. The user needs to upgrade to Pro or Enterprise.

prompt: Which command would a technician use to view all active network connections and listening ports on a Windows PC?
explanation: netstat -an shows all active connections (ESTABLISHED) and listening ports. Useful for detecting malware that has opened unexpected ports or connections to C2 servers.

prompt: What is the BEST defense against ransomware?
explanation: Offline backups (3-2-1: 3 copies, 2 media types, 1 off-site) are the best ransomware defense. Antivirus helps prevent infection but cannot undo encryption. Off-site backups survive local ransomware attacks.

prompt: A technician is asked to securely dispose of hard drives containing sensitive medical records. Which method is MOST appropriate?

options.text: Delete all files and format the drive

explanation: For sensitive data (PHI, PII), physical destruction (shredding, crushing) or degaussing (magnetic erasure) is required. Simply formatting or deleting does not remove data — it can be recovered. Overwriting 7+ times may also be acceptable.

prompt: A computer shows a BSOD (Blue Screen of Death) with a MEMORY_MANAGEMENT error. What is the MOST likely cause?
explanation: MEMORY_MANAGEMENT BSODs indicate RAM issues — faulty RAM sticks, bad RAM slots, or incompatible RAM. Run Windows Memory Diagnostic (mdsched.exe) to test. Also check for recently installed drivers.

prompt: What does the acronym EFS stand for in Windows security?
explanation: EFS (Encrypting File System) encrypts individual files and folders on NTFS volumes. It's tied to the user's Windows login. Different from BitLocker which encrypts the entire drive.

prompt: A technician is setting up a new PC and needs to support drives larger than 2TB with UEFI firmware. Which partition scheme should they use?
explanation: GPT (GUID Partition Table) supports drives larger than 2TB and is required by UEFI firmware. MBR is limited to 2TB drives and 4 primary partitions — use it only with legacy BIOS.

prompt: Which of the following BEST describes a man-in-the-middle (MITM) attack?

options.text: Intercepting communication between two parties without their knowledge
Guessing passwords through trial and error
Sending fake emails impersonating a company

explanation: MITM attacks intercept communications between two parties (e.g., between a user and a website). Can capture credentials, manipulate data. Prevented by TLS/HTTPS, VPN, certificate validation.

prompt: A user reports that every time they open their browser, a new homepage appears that they did not set. What is the MOST likely cause?

options.text: A Windows update changed the settings

explanation: A browser hijacker is malware (often adware) that modifies browser settings — homepage, default search, new tab page. Remove: check browser extensions, reset browser, run Malwarebytes.
